I dip dive into `wait` module and read the functionality and test the it on my local so here how it works with `Until` in simple words:
```
	delayFunc := wait.Backoff{
		Duration: 10 * time.Millisecond,
		Cap:      15 * time.Second,
		Factor:   2.0,
		Steps:    11}.DelayFunc()
```
Loops over `Steps` and multiply `Duration` to `Factor` in each iteration. And waits for `C()` function which works with `Duration`, it ends increasing when hits the `Cap`. So here it increases until 15 seconds and get 15 second on each invoke of `delayFunc`. And i was wrong about `DelayWithReset ` we don't need it.

issue_context.title: Implement checking etcd version to warn about deprecated etcd versions
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Part of https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2340

From https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/2340-Consistent-reads-from-cache/README.md#bug-in-etcd-progress-notification

> Only recently community discovered a bug https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/15220 for requesting progress notification. This bug causes a race between sending an event and progress notification with the same revision. Normally we would expect to event to always come first, however due to the bug, progress notification might be sent first. Serving a consistent lists in that situation could result in returning too early and missing the event. The bug was only fixed in v3.4.25 and v3.5.8 (both 9 months old), which is too fresh for Kubernetes to not handle.
> 
> Our tests have shown that with the bug manual progress notification cannot be trusted at all. It causes a silent corruption that cannot be automatically detected prior to acting upon the corrupted data. For Beta, we propose to conditionally enable the feature in a way that mitigates the risk of unaware users stumbling on the bug.
> 
> We propose to implement a safeguard that will prevent enabling ConsistentListFromCache on etcd version with broken progress notification. During kube-apiserver startup we will verify etcd version by calling Status method and checking etcd patch version. The condition will only pass if all etcd endpoints have etcd version that includes the fix for https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/15220.
> 
> The proposed behavior of the safeguard for Beta:
> 
> etcd version could not be acquired or etcd new enough - warn, but continue with whatever the current value of the feature gate is
> * etcd too old, feature gate not explicitly specified - warn and disable the feature
> * etcd too old, feature gate explicitly enabled - abort
> * etcd new enough - use whatever the current value of the feature gate is
>
> The proposed behavior of the safeguard for GA (feature gate locked to true):
> * etcd version could not be acquired - warn, but continue with the feature enabled
> * etcd too old - abort
> * etcd new enough - enable feature
> 
> Checking etcd version during start should be a good enough solution as we generally don't expect etcd clusters to downgrade. As of etcd v3.5 it is not an officially supported feature.

For now posted as a "help wanted" issue, however if we cannot hit the timeline for 1.30 code freeze ([5th March](https://github.com/kubernetes/sig-release/tree/master/releases/release-1.30#summary)) I would take it over so we don't miss. Still issue is simple enough that it can be quickly implemented.

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted
/help

### Why is this needed?

Warn users about running on buggy etcd version

review_comments:
Note: Checking each endpoint independently means that decision whether etcd is supported will be reached just after the first endpoint from cluster responds instead of waiting for all of them. 

Still I think that's ok, because we expect endpoints from a single cluster to give the same response, as all members should have the same etcd version. This even bring one benefit. In etcd you only need 2 out of 3 cluster members to be healthy for cluster to work. So this change makes it work if one etcd member is permanently down.
Handle error right after getting it.
Done
I'm not sure if you've already discussed this, but should users of this method be able to distinguish between `not supported` and `I don’t yet know because I haven’t been able to check`?

We use `progressNotifySupported    *bool` for that reason, but either we should wait for all clients to been checked or return `false`. And waiting for all clients is not applicable here. One other solution might be returning `*bool` from here but i'm not confident enough about it (not sure we can or not as this is a good practice or not), and also needs approval from @wojtek-t and @serathius too.

> I'm not sure if you've already discussed this, but should users of this method be able to distinguish between `not supported` and `I don’t yet know because I haven’t been able to check`?

How that distinction would be used by user? In case of consistent reads, we don't need it.

Let's assume that I would like to request a bookmark for the purpose of initializing some object. If I could distinguish between the states, then I would know whether to wait for information from the checker or not.

More specifically, such functionality would be useful to fix https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124754#discussion_r1594063439
`purpose of initializing some object.` can you clarify what do you mean by that?

We found a bug in the cacher, it won't deliver bookmark events until it receives an event from the underlying storage. We were thinking about scheduling at least one progress notification request so that the cacher is primed. Knowing whether the version/feature checker has been initialised would help in this scenario.
Ok, I would need more context to understand the case more. Can you send me a issue number?

I think there is relatively non-invasive change to make it work for the StreamingList scenario too. But let's proceeed with unblocking at least consistent lists and we will make it work for streaming lists as a followup.
OK, if you don't mind, could you shed some light on the potential solution here?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124754/files#r1596607679

OK, this seems to solve one case. I wonder what would happen in a situation where a watch request actually requires progress notification. In that case changing the state from `on` to `off` might/will be problematic - the request will wait for the notification which might not come to the server.
We should be able to catch that at runtime and fail the request in such case. This should be extremely rare (it literally should never happen) and for that reason I believe it's fine.
Regarding Lukasz' comment, the last three lines of this comment should also be copied to the comment of Supports() method.
Done.

By checking only the `supported` variable the state can flap from `on` to `off` which is not ideal.

Also, I think I've asked this question before (but I cannot find it). 
The doc for the `Supports` says `Returns true if all endpoints in etcd clients are supporting the feature`.
I think that the `clientSupportsRequestWatchProgress` method doesn't ensure that.

> By checking only the supported variable the state can flap from on to off which is not ideal.

You cannot avoid it without blocking apiserver start on all etcd instances being available.
Please take a look at tests we have a few scenarios for that.

> Also, I think I've asked this question before (but I cannot find it). The doc for the `Supports` says `Returns true if all endpoints in etcd clients are supporting the feature`. I think that the `clientSupportsRequestWatchProgress` method doesn't ensure that.

Can you be more specific? We have a test for that, if we miss something we would need to more context to fix it.

I am concerned about the dynamic nature of the function itself.
The fact that it can be set to `on` for arbitrary time and then to `off`.
It’s also about not really knowing the number of endpoints we are waiting for.
The fact that checking some endpoints may fail (error) and about the fact that I am not able to tell whether the checker is still initialising or if the feature is not supported.
This behavior is enough for consistent reads from cache. If there is a change if `supported` the only bad effect would be very short time where APF calculations were incorrect.

Today I know that without this feature, in some cases when streaming is used, the server might deadlock. So it would be useful to know whether this feature is supported or not so that streaming could be disabled.

Ok, makes sense that streaming will need some different approach, but let's not try to solve all the problems at the same time. When we have consistent lists from cache working we would be happy to help with WatchList.
From what I've managed to figure out so far, solving this problem won't be easy and might even require changing the entire approach/implementation :(
Let's unblock one of the features and not block both..

This log is redundant with 
```
klog.Info("RequestWatchProgress feature is not supported by provided etcd. This will prevent ConsistentListFromCache from working")
```

I was thinking about logging errors from etcd, however that may be unnecessary as if etcd is unavailable, all other requests will be failing too and logging.
I would live this one - and remove the other one - added a comment there.
Thanks, done.
why not use `runtime.HandleError` ?
I'm not sure if this error here need to be sent to sever for analysis.
because only happens when we shutdown etcd context.
